title: True or False?
description: Meet Booleans, the binary wizards who only speak in absolute truths and falsehoods!

content.value: In Python, there is a special data type called a Boolean. Booleans are named after a mathematician named George Boole. The best part? Booleans are extremely simple: they can only ever be True or False!
We can use special comparison operators to ask the computer questions. The computer will always answer with True or False!

- `>`: Is it greater than?
- `<`: Is it less than?
- `==`: Are they EXACTLY equal? (Notice we use two equals signs `==` to compare, and one equals sign `=` to put things in a variable box!)
- `!=`: Are they NOT equal?

print(5 > 3)    # Prints True
print(2 == 4)   # Prints False
print(10 != 9)  # Prints True
In Python, the first letters of True and False must ALWAYS be capitalized. Writing 'true' or 'false' in lowercase will make the computer throw a tantrum!

practice.question: Create a variable called 'my_guess' and check if 8 is equal to 8. Print your variable!

quiz.question: Which symbol do we use to check if two values are equal?
